newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian tax deal seen easing fiscal pressure.
newsitem.headline: Italian tax deal seen easing fiscal pressure.

text.p: Parties supporting Italy's centre-left government have reached a deal over a reform of the tax system which should lead to a lower-than-expected increase in fiscal pressure next year, newspaper commentators said.

The accord, thrashed out at a late night sitting of a parliamentary budget commission on Friday, included an agreement to lower the planned tax rate for a new regional tax (IREP) and cut the number of bands for income tax (IRPEF).

It also introduced a new wording for the planned 1997 "Euro-Tax", which means the government can now use savings from lower debt servicing costs to cushion the impact of the as yet unspecified fiscal measures.
"The new taxes will be less heavy," daily Corriere della Sera said in a front page headline.

The 1997 budget is designed to cut 62.5 trillion lire from next year's deficit. Some 12.5 trillion lire of this was designed to come from the one-off "Euro Tax", which is hoped will boost Italy's chances of becoming a founder member of the planned single European currency.

But the new description of the tax, which will be voted on in the lower house of parliament next month, says revenue will be raised by a "one-off contribution from incomes, excluding the lowest incomes, and from savings of a financial nature."

La Repubblica newspaper said the wording indicated that the government would include in the so-called "Euro Tax" some two to three trillion lire of revenues saved by lower-than-expected interest payable on state bills and floating certificates.
Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said the government would not take into account any fall in market rates.
"The phrase 'savings of a financial nature' means that resources can be found in a different fashion," Ciampi was quoted as saying by the Italian news agency Ansa on Saturday.

"In no way has the government calculated in its budget sums the positive performance of interest rates...However some added support for the budget can come from this direction, i.e. from financial savings," he added.
The Bank of Italy cut its official discount rate to 7.5 percent last week from 8.25 percent.
The government's proposals to overhaul the country's complex and leaking fiscal system created strong tensions within Prime Minister Romano Prodi's six-month old coalition.

Under pressure from Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini's Italian Renewal party, the Finance Ministry agreed to reduce the weight of the new IREP, setting the maximum rate for the regional tax at between 3.5 and 4.5 percent instead of five percent.
The Finance Ministry also bowed to pressure from the hard left Communist Refoundation and modified plans aimed at streamlining income tax.

The original proposals, which the government insisted would have a neutral impact on revenues, suggested reducing the number of tax brackets from seven to five and raising the minimum income tax rate to 20 percent from 10 percent and cutting the maximum rate to 46 percent from 51 percent.
Under the compromise solution, approved by the budget committee, the tax brackets will still be reduced to five, but no mention will be made of exactly how this will be done.
"However, there is a formal undertaking that the tax rate for people on low to middle incomes will not be increased," Refoundation's parliamentary party leader, Oliviero Diliberto, told reporters.
Italy's draft 1997 budget will be submitted to the full lower house on October 30 with a final vote due by November 14.
